acceptance.goalCondition: `node factory.mjs verify <agent-dir>` exits 0: every code acceptance criterion is PASS against the run's own artifacts (paused-publish, batch-volume, destination-clean, copy-unique, not-blocked) and every human criterion is PARKED at its named gate with a signed-off review artifact. A blocked run (pipeline exit 2, report.json blocked=true) is never done.

criteria.description: Every ad in the batch is created PAUSED. Nothing the agent writes can spend on its own.
criteria.verification: code: every <creative_id>/publish.json payload.ad.fields.status === 'PAUSED' AND report.json.all_paused === true.
criteria.negativeCase: A payload whose ad.fields.status is 'ACTIVE' (or a report with all_paused=false) FAILS the check.

criteria.description: The batch published the agreed number of creatives (nothing silently dropped).
criteria.verification: code: count of non-skipped creatives in database.json === params.expected, else creative.statics_per_day + creative.videos_per_day. params.expected=2 pins the DRY_RUN fixture batch (fixtures/creatives.json), which is fixture-driven, not generated, because pipeline.mjs's live creative generation is not wired yet. DELETE params.expected once it is, so the check grades against the real configured daily cap.
criteria.negativeCase: A database.json with fewer (or more) non-skipped creatives than expected FAILS.

criteria.description: Every ad points at the real configured landing page: no empty link, no TODO, no example.com, no foreign host.
criteria.verification: code: every database.json creatives[].destination_link is non-empty, free of 'TODO'/'example.com', and its host is one of the configured landing hosts.

criteria.description: No two creatives in the batch ship identical ad copy (the classic same-prompt-N-renders generator failure).
criteria.verification: code: the object_story_spec message in each <creative_id>/publish.json payload is distinct across the batch.
criteria.negativeCase: Two creatives whose payload message strings are identical FAIL.

criteria.description: The run actually published something: a batch where every creative was held at the human_review gate is BLOCKED, not done.
criteria.verification: code: report.json.blocked !== true (pipeline.mjs exits 2 on a fully-blocked run).
criteria.negativeCase: A fixture batch with no creative approved -> report.blocked=true, pipeline exit 2, criterion FAILS.

criteria.description: A human reviewer signed off the creative batch: on-brand, on-persona, on-message, and safe to spend behind.
criteria.verification: human gate 'reviewer' (Shot B): the reviewer approves the batch against creatives/<date>/database.json + the rendered assets, and sets human_review.status='approved' per creative. Never self-graded by the agent that generated the creative.

criteria.description: Each rendered creative passed vision QA against the brand rubric (layout rules, no rendering artifacts, no banned marks).
criteria.verification: External verifier: vision-qa.mjs sends each rendered image + the config.brand rubric to a vision model (default claude-opus-4-8; env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and writes <runDir>/<creative_id>/vision-review.json with provenance (model, gradedAt, imageSha256). The registered 'vision-qa' check grades ONLY those artifacts: status must be 'passed' AND the imageSha256 must re-hash to the image on disk. Verdicts without provenance (the fixture-constant pattern) FAIL. With no artifacts yet the check reports PENDING, never PASS - live creative generation is still unwired.
criteria.negativeCase: test/vision-qa.test.mjs: a 'failed' verdict FAILS; a 'passed' verdict missing model/gradedAt/imageSha256 FAILS (fixture-constant); a verdict whose imageSha256 does not match the image on disk FAILS.

rules: Real product UI screenshot with one bold headline; no stock photography
Flat, institutional, credible; no gradients or startup gloss
Plain background, one verbatim-style buyer quote in large type
Reads like an internal district email, not an ad
30-second talking-head; hook in first 3 seconds; one CTA
Speaker persona matches the buyer, not a young influencer

personas.descriptor: Director of Professional Learning at a district or ESA running registration season on spreadsheets and a Google Form; the state recertification report takes a week
Registrar / Director of Student Services with paper packets in a filing cabinet and a school-choice lottery someone runs in Excel and defends to the board
Curriculum & Instruction Director who cannot prove the coaching investment produced anything; coaches log in shared drives
CCR&R Executive Director running intake, provider lists, referral history, and state reporting across four disconnected systems
Superintendent / Executive Director who asks about outcomes, security, and FERPA, not features; has never heard of us
Administrator on CourseWhere or an old Wisdomwhere since 2009; nobody left knows how it works; terrified of a migration disaster

insights.pain_point: Registration season costs the team six weeks of manual admin
When the state asks for Act 48 / SCECH / CTLE hours, the answer is a week-long project instead of a button
Agencies buy what a named peer agency in their state already runs
Burned by acquisitions and forced migrations; Frontline bought MyLearningPlan, Pearson sunset Schoolnet
No budget for a platform commitment; need one problem solved by August
Enterprise vendors are a ticket queue; a published phone number a certified human answers is the pitch
Getting off an aging system without breaking thirty years of records
The school-choice lottery must be re-runnable with the same result in front of the board

brand.mission: Four things education agencies do every year. One platform that does them.
brand.audience: Directors of professional learning, registrars, coaching coordinators, and CCR&R directors at US public education agencies (districts, ISDs, IUs, ESCs, BOCES, CCR&Rs)
brand.tone: Plain, specific, institutional. Short sentences. No hype, no feature lists, no exclamation marks.
message_pillars: Independent since 1996 - never acquired, no forced migrations
Buy one module, not a suite
A published phone number a certified specialist answers
generation_rules: NEVER use stock photography of children - it teaches the algorithm to find parents instead of administrators
Show the real product where possible
No two ads in a batch share a headline
No invented statistics; the only numbers allowed are: since 1996, 33+ states, 80% less registration admin time
